narrative:
The prediction estimated a 66.8% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. Because the application review treated that as a likely bar-failure risk, your law school application was denied. This does not mean you cannot succeed; it means the information considered pointed more strongly toward failure than passing.

Your Year 3 class standing was the strongest factor behind that result. You were recorded in the first decile, while accepted students averaged near the sixth decile, and this factor pushed the prediction toward failure. Your Year 1 standing was the second most influential factor; it was also in the first decile, versus an average around the sixth decile for accepted students, and it likewise pushed toward failure. Your undergraduate GPA was the third most important factor but worked in your favor: at 3.60, it is above the accepted-student average of about 3.23, pushing the prediction toward passing. Even so, it did not outweigh the concerns raised by your year-by-year class standings.

To strengthen a future application, focus on explaining and improving the academic record behind those standings, seek pre-law advising, and consider whether additional coursework, legal work experience, or retaking the LSAT would demonstrate readiness. Request feedback from the program, address the bar-risk concern directly, and reapply only after you can show a stronger recent academic trajectory.
